candidates.attacker_control: Complete control of parsing input: the JSON/parser token stream (e.g. an HTTP request body deserialized with a Jackson mapper) determines the number of `[` wrapping a scalar, i.e. the recursion depth. No privileged position or local access is needed; only the target type and the (non-default) feature configuration are app-side preconditions.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) Verified the same unwrap pattern IS guarded in three sibling places, so this is a missing-check defect rather than intended behaviour: `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue` lines 357-367 rejects nested `START_ARRAY`, `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` lines 632-640 rejects it with the 'deeply-nested Array' message, and the wrapper-typed number/boolean deserializers route `ID_START_ARRAY` to `_deserializeFromArray` (NumberDeserializers.java:299-300, 391-392, 481-482, 522, 629-630, 726-727, 815-816, 943-944, 1013-1014) and are therefore not reachable. 2) Confirmed the unguarded calls are genuine self-recursion reaching the same method on the next token (source text at the cited lines; index self-CALLS edges at StdDeserializer.java:723/417/586 are navigation hints only and were verified in source). 3) Checked that no other mitigation exists in this snapshot: no `_depth`/`getNestingDepth`/`StreamReadConstraints` reference anywhere under src/main/java, and jackson-core 2.14 (`pom.xml` `${jackson.version.core}`) has no nesting-depth constraint. 4) Checked that plain untyped `Object` targets are covered by the non-recursive `UntypedObjectDeserializerNR` (UntypedObjectDeserializer.java:196-200), so that path was not counted as exposed. 5) Feature is off by default, so exposure depends on non-default app configuration - stated explicitly in prerequisites rather than assumed. 6) No build, test or exploit was executed; StackOverflowError was not observed at runtime and the byte-size threshold is not measured.
candidates.impact: Denial of service: an attacker-supplied payload of deeply nested arrays (tens of thousands of `[` wrapping a scalar, well within normal request sizes) exhausts the JVM thread stack while parsing, producing `StackOverflowError`. This is an `Error`, so it is not converted to `JsonMappingException` and is normally not caught by application `catch (Exception)`/`catch (IOException)` handlers; the request thread dies (and repeated requests allow sustained denial of service). Successful parses are not required - exhaustion happens before the end-of-array validation could reject the payload.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) The application enables `DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS` (false by default, `DeserializationFeature.java:326`) on the mapper used for untrusted input. 2) The bound target is a value type that takes the unguarded path: a primitive-typed (or primitive array element) `boolean`/`byte`/`short`/`int`/`long`/`float`/`double` property or root value, a `java.util.Date`-typed value, or a builder-based POJO (`@JsonDeserialize(builder=...)`). Wrapper types on the same properties are protected because they route through `_deserializeFromArray` -> `_deserializeWrappedValue`. 3) The underlying jackson-core in use has no maximum nesting depth (this snapshot predates `StreamReadConstraints`; no reference exists in the tree).
candidates.root_cause: When `DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS` is enabled, the unwrap branch consumes one `START_ARRAY` (`p.nextToken()`) and then re-invokes the same deserialization routine on whatever follows it, without validating that the following token is not itself another `START_ARRAY`. The check that the maintainers use elsewhere is absent here: `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue` (lines 355-369) explicitly fails when the current token is `START_ARRAY`, and `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` (lines 631-645, comment dated 23-Aug-2022) explicitly rejects a second nested array. Because the recursive call happens before any end-of-array validation (`_verifyEndArrayForSingle` runs only after the nested call returns), recursion depth is exactly the attacker-supplied JSON array nesting depth, with no limit anywhere in the library (no depth counter, no `getNestingDepth`, no `StreamReadConstraints` in this snapshot).
candidates.title: Unbounded recursion in UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS handling (primitive value deserializers and BuilderBasedDeserializer) allows stack exhaustion / denial of service
candidates.trace: Primitive path: `ObjectMapper.readValue` -> property deserializer `NumberDeserializers.IntegerDeserializer.deserialize` (NumberDeserializers.java:525-531, `_primitive` -> `_parseIntPrimitive`) -> `StdDeserializer._parseIntPrimitive` case `JsonTokenId.ID_START_ARRAY` (StdDeserializer.java:720-725) -> `p.nextToken(); _parseIntPrimitive(p, ctxt)` (line 723) -> repeats once per nested `[` (`_verifyEndArrayForSingle` is only reached after the deepest call returns). Identical self-recursion edges exist for `_parseBooleanPrimitive` (line 417), `_parseBytePrimitive` (line 586), `_parseShortPrimitive` (line 656), `_parseLongPrimitive` (line 874), `_parseFloatPrimitive` (line 1007), `_parseDoublePrimitive` (line 1136) - confirmed in source text and corroborated by the index's self-CALLS edges. Date path: `DateDeserializers` -> `_parseDate` case `ID_START_ARRAY` (line 1288) -> `_parseDateFromArray` (line 1297) -> `_parseDate` (line 1316) recursion. Builder path: `BuilderBasedDeserializer.deserialize` case `ID_START_ARRAY` (line 234-237) -> `_deserializeFromArray` (line 499) -> unwrap branch (lines 528-534) `deserialize(p, ctxt)` re-enters on the still-`START_ARRAY` token, whereas the equivalent `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` line 634 first checks `p.nextToken() == JsonToken.START_ARRAY` and fails. Net effect for all three paths: uncaught `StackOverflowError` during parsing of a deeply wrapped scalar.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: recursion depth needed to overflow a real stack, payload sizes, and whether a given deployment catches `StackOverflowError` were not tested. Reachability of every listed primitive method from a remote request depends on the application's target types (verified by source for POJO/root primitive and builder targets, not for every entry point). The precise location/scope of the upstream fix is unknown; the `BuilderBasedDeserializer` site is included as the same root cause (twin of the already-guarded `BeanDeserializer` method), not as a separately confirmed defect. Float/double/date paths were traced but not exhaustively cross-checked against every subtype (`DateDeserializers` subclasses, primitive array element paths). Test sources are absent from this snapshot, so intended-behaviour confirmation via tests was impossible.
candidates.weakness_type: Uncontrolled recursion / resource exhaustion (CWE-674, stack exhaustion DoS)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 18,045 model-visible files; binary/NUL files skipped by policy (none relevant), no >5 MiB files, no symlink/sensitive-name exclusions; parity with the B0 filters. The tree is jackson-databind 2.14.0-SNAPSHOT: src/main/java (472 files, ~464 under com/fasterxml/jackson/databind) plus non-executable docs/javadoc HTML for 1.9 and 2.10, attic/, .github/, pom.xml and Maven wrapper. Notably, src/test is absent from this snapshot, so no test-based validation was possible. Relation index: complete (all 18,045 files indexed, hash parity, no dropped files), but syntax/navigation-level only (no data-flow, no runtime reachability, no SAST oracle; build/tests not run) - every edge used was re-verified against source text. Inspected in depth: deser/BeanDeserializer.java, deser/BuilderBasedDeserializer.java, deser/std/StdDeserializer.java, deser/std/NumberDeserializers.java, deser/std/FromStringDeserializer.java, deser/std/StackTraceElementDeserializer.java, deser/std/PrimitiveArrayDeserializers.java, deser/std/StringArrayDeserializer.java, deser/std/UntypedObjectDeserializer(NR).java, deser/impl/ExternalTypeHandler.java, deser/SettableAnyProperty.java, node/NodeSerialization.java, util/TokenBuffer.java (spot), type/TypeFactory.java (spot), jsontype/impl/SubTypeValidator.java (spot). Not exhaustively reviewed: ser/** serializers, most of introspect/** and type/**, remaining deser/** files, all docs/javadoc HTML, files whose only signal was an index navigation hint.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so intended behaviour/regression expectations for UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS could not be checked and no test-based confirmation exists.

The P1 relation index provides syntax-level navigation candidates only; it proves no data flow, reachability or exploitability, and several of its name-based 'security_call' facts pointed at benign code.
Nothing was compiled, executed or fuzzed: the StackOverflowError outcome is inferred from the recursion structure in source, not runtime-observed, and no payload-size threshold was measured.

Exploitability is configuration-dependent: the global DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS must be enabled by the application (non-default), and the attacker-controlled value must be bound to one of the affected target types; deployments with default configuration are not affected.
The exact upstream fix's location/scope is unknown from this snapshot, and the BuilderBasedDeserializer site is presented as the same root cause rather than an independently confirmed defect.
Large parts of the library (ser/**, introspect/**, type/**, most deser/** and all bundled javadoc HTML) were not read line-by-line, so an unrelated stronger issue in those areas cannot be ruled out.

Contains an explicit allocation guard (LONGEST_EAGER_ALLOC = 100_000, comment referencing databind#3328) and is only reachable through JDK native deserialization of Jackson node classes, which is not the Jackson attacker-input path.

No source evidence of a new bypass or missing validation in this snapshot, so this remains a speculative hardening lead rather than a finding.

summary: Repository is jackson-databind 2.14.0-SNAPSHOT (~late Aug 2022 development state; newest dated source comment 23-Aug-2022). Review focused on the deserialization attack surface where default typing/coercion features make attacker JSON reach library code. The strongest source-supported issue is a missing nesting guard in the `DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS` ("single-value array wrapping") code path: several deserializers re-enter themselves on the next token without ever checking whether that token is *another* array, so recursion depth equals attacker-controlled JSON array nesting depth and ends in StackOverflowError (uncontrolled resource consumption). The snapshot itself shows the intended validation elsewhere: `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue` (lines 355-369, 2017 comment "specifically block recursive resolution ... to cause infinite looping") and `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` (lines 631-645, 23-Aug-2022 comment "To prevent unbounded nested arrays ... check there is NOT another START_ARRAY lurking there"). The unguarded sites are the primitive-value paths (`StdDeserializer._parseBooleanPrimitive/_parseBytePrimitive/_parseShortPrimitive/_parseIntPrimitive/_parseLongPrimitive/_parseFloatPrimitive/_parseDoublePrimitive`, and the `java.util.Date` path `_parseDateFromArray` -> `_parseDate`) plus `BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray`, which is the direct twin of the guarded `BeanDeserializer` method. The primitive-vs-wrapper asymmetry is visible in `NumberDeserializers`: wrapper `Byte/Short/Character/Float/Double/BigInteger/BigDecimal/Integer/Long/Boolean` route START_ARRAY to `_deserializeFromArray` (guarded), while the `_primitive == true` variants call the unguarded `_parseXxxPrimitive` self-recursion. No depth counter, `getNestingDepth` or `StreamReadConstraints` exists anywhere in this snapshot, so nothing else caps the recursion. Runtime behaviour was not executed; the finding is a static code-evidence lead. Non-array-related index hints (ObjectMapper/ObjectWriter/SequenceWriter/TokenBuffer/NodeSerialization/DefaultSerializerProvider "security_call" facts) were checked and rejected as benign.
